**The meaning of the verses**
﴿إِذْ أَقْسَمُوا لَيَصْرِمُنَّهَا مُصْبِحِينَ﴾ ﴿وَلَا يَسْتَثْنُونَ﴾
… just as We tested the owners of the garden when they swore among themselves that they would surely cut the fruit of their garden early in the morning, so that no one but them, of the poor and the like, would eat from it; and they did not say: "In sha Allah."

﴿أَن لَّا يَدْخُلَنَّهَا الْيَوْمَ عَلَيْكُم مِّسْكِينٌ﴾
So they hurried off, whispering to one another: Do not let any of the needy get into your garden today.

﴿عَسَىٰ رَبُّنَا أَن يُبْدِلَنَا خَيْرًا مِّنْهَا إِنَّا إِلَىٰ رَبِّنَا رَاغِبُونَ﴾
When they saw their garden burnt, they did not recognise it and said: "We have lost our way to it." When they realised that it was their garden, they said: "No, rather we have been deprived of its good, because we were set on stinginess and on keeping the poor away." … Perhaps our Lord will give us something better than our garden, because of our repentance and our admission of our sin. To our Lord alone we turn with longing, hoping for forgiveness and seeking good.

📖 At-Tafsir Al-Muyassar — King Fahd Complex.

**Talk with your child**
1. What did the good father use to do on harvest day? And what did his sons decide after him? And why did they set off in the dark, speaking in low voices?
2. They swore that they would pick it and did not say "In sha Allah." Why do we say it when we decide to do something tomorrow? (Because tomorrow is in Allah's hands, not ours. And it is not said to escape a promise we do not intend to keep.)
3. When they saw their garden black and burnt, did they lose hope? What did they say, and what did they hope for from their Lord?

**This week's exercise**
"The poor person's share": whenever something good comes into your home this week — fruit, sweets or pocket money — your child sets aside a share of it themselves for someone in need, a worker or a neighbour, and hands it to them with their right hand.
